analysis.title: Global Rates Weekly: Hawk affAIr
key_insights: BofA stays underweight the US front end and in flatteners after the hot October CPI and a hawkish shift in Fed speakers. Over the past week the 2Y yield rose 40bp and the 10Y rose 25bp, driven by payrolls, CPI and Fed hawks.

The market prices about a 10% chance of a 50bp Fed hike in December. BofA says not to fade it. A 50bp move becomes more likely if November unemployment is 4.0%, November average hourly earnings are 0.4% m/m, and tech sentiment stabilizes.

Consensus has shifted on the Iran de-escalation view and on the central bank cycle being well priced. Waller said a 50bp hike 'should be considered' and Logan said 'move more rapidly'. BofA expects Fed Chair Warsh to sound hawkish next time he speaks on policy.

BofA attributes part of the rates sell-off to unwinds of long or received front-end positions. These positions rebuilt with a short-vol bias after equities stabilized. The unwind amplified the sell-off and the curve flattening.

BofA's pay front-end bias rests on three points: 3m annualized core CPI is back to early 2024 levels, front-end pricing lags the shift in Fed rhetoric, and a Taylor rule implies fed funds at 5%+. Core services CPI (3m/3m annualized) is back at about 4%.

BofA says long-term inflation pricing looks complacent. 5y5y real rates are much higher than after the financial crisis and 5y5y inflation is much lower, so the October CPI supports the real-curve flattener.

The US debt limit is likely to bind in Feb '27, with a projected X-date in Nov '27. BofA expects Treasury to guide to an August X-date. The TGA should draw down and bills should be cut from March '27, which richens bills and pushes funding lower. BofA recommends long M7 3m SOFR/FF and closes long Dec '26 SOFR/FF.

BofA expects a higher US rates-vol regime in 2027, with 1y10y fair value near 90-95bp and an 80-105bp range. It favors 2s10s floor ladders, receiver spreads and calendars in the belly, and scaling into short left vs right vol.

In Europe, BofA enters a received 2y1y OIS position at 3.15% (target 2.6%, stop 3.46%). It closes the 6m2y vs 18m2y receiver calendar and the short 3m2y EU vs US vol at target. It keeps the 3m2y receiver 1x2. The thesis is that ECB downside growth risks and tight conditions support cuts in the next two years.

BofA expects the Eurosystem balance sheet to fall to €5.9trn by YE26 and €5.7trn by YE27. Excess liquidity should fall to €2.0trn and €1.8trn, and OMO take-up should rise to €70bn and €350bn. Structural portfolios are not expected near term.

In Australia, BofA recommends U7/U8 bill flatteners (entry -23bp, target -50bp, stop -6bp) and a 2s5s BBSW/SOFR basis flattener (entry 2.5bp, target 0.5bp, stop 4bp). It expects the next RBA move to be a cut in H2-27. December OIS pricing is about 1bp and could rise toward 5bp on hawkish minutes and a strong jobs print.

In Japan, BofA estimates JGB futures positioning is long-biased (Z-score about +1.3). Longs have an average unrealized gain of ¥1.06 and shorts an average unrealized loss of ¥1.45. A further rise in JGB futures could force short covering.

Technical view: the US 10Y yield held uptrend support at 4.81-4.83% and rebounded above 5.05% after CPI. BofA favors a renewed uptrend, with a break above 5.17% targeting a retest of the YTD high of 5.36%. Ideally yield stays above 4.99% or 4.86%.

UK inflation and labour data next week could change the 19bp priced for a December BoE hike. BofA's economists' base case remains a February hike. BofA thinks the totality of hikes priced is somewhat excessive.

risk_factors: A hawkish Fed repricing or 50bp December hike could extend the front-end sell-off and curve flattening.
An early debt limit resolution, or a hawkish Fed balance sheet policy, would hurt the long M7 SOFR/FF trade.
Stronger than expected euro area growth would hurt the received 2y1y OIS position.
Higher energy and gas prices could renew pressure on EUR rates.
A strong AU CPI print or hawkish RBA minutes could pressure the AU flatteners.
Weak Kangaroo issuance in Q1-27 is a risk to the AUD basis flattener.
An equity sell-off with poor long-end liquidity is a risk to the long 10y20y inflation swap.
charts_described: Exhibit 6 shows the 10y z-score of one-day UST 2y yield changes, labelled the largest one-day sell-off in 2y yields since April 2025.
Exhibit 5 shows core services CPI (3m/3m annualized) back at 4%.
Exhibit 9 is a Taylor rule grid. Spot unemployment and core PCE imply fed funds near 5.25%.
vol_and_positioning: BofA expects a higher US rates-vol regime in '27, with 1y10y fair value around 90-95bp and an 80-105bp range. It says these levels have historically been adverse for risk assets.
It favors 2s10s floor ladders, long receiver spreads and calendars in the belly, and scaling into short left vs right side vol.
Long front-end positioning rebuilt with a short-vol bias earlier this week and likely amplified the sell-off.
The 2Y yield had its largest one-day sell-off since April 2025 (10y z-score of one-day changes, Exhibit 6).
The 2s10s bear-flattening frequency (CAF) was below 15-20% in late Oct and early Nov and has since picked up. Over 40-45% would mean bear flattening is overpriced.
In the EUR market, BofA closes the short 3m2y EU vs US vol and the 6m2y vs 18m2y receiver calendar at target. EUR vol is expected to be supported into YE26 and lower in 2027.
JGB futures positioning is long-biased (Z-score about +1.3). Shorts hold average unrealized losses of ¥1.45, and BofA sees a risk of short covering.
geopolitical: Iran de-escalation view has faded after Trump said 'we don't need a deal with Iran'.
BofA notes higher energy and gas prices as a risk to EUR rates, and says the persistent energy shock weighs on euro area growth.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA argues a 50bp hike becomes more likely if unemployment is 4.0%, average hourly earnings are 0.4% m/m and tech sentiment stabilizes. It says it is better to address mistakes early. Waller said 50bp 'should be considered' and Logan said to 'move more rapidly'.
tension_points.bear_case: Clients push back that a 50bp December hike would imply the October hold was a mistake. The market prices only about 10%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: November unemployment staying above 4.0% or hourly earnings below 0.4% m/m, or weak data removing expected hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: BofA argues the ECB acknowledges downside growth risks from the energy shock and tight financial conditions. This supports cuts in the next two years, so 2y1y should sell off less than shorter forwards.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher gas prices and stronger EA growth data could push 2y1y yields higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Stronger than expected euro area growth data, with a stop at 3.46% on the 2y1y OIS.

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation data and Fed rhetoric support paying the front end and flattening the curve, and the 50bp hike risk should not be faded.
A binding debt limit leads to TGA drawdowns and bill cuts, which pushes funding rates lower and richens bills.
theme_stances.evidence: We like long M7 SOFR/ FF.

theme_stances.key_argument: The market prices rate cuts in the coming two years, which supports receiving 2y1y OIS after the sell-off.
